subject: POC Trial: model selection & evaluation plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Carolyn Wu <carolyn@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC Trial: model selection & evaluation plan

Hi Carolyn,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to hear more about ACME's search & answering use case for customer-facing knowledge. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

1) Success criteria (as discussed):
- Precision/recall on our benchmark: target F1 >= 0.78 on your sample intents.
- Multilingual support: primary coverage for English, French, Spanish with comparable accuracy (delta <= 5% vs English).
- Latency: p95 generation <= 800ms for 2k-token requests under trial capacity.
- Cost: target cost per 1k tokens under the trial < $4 (to be validated).

2) Evaluation plan & ownership:
- Redwood will run the trial models against your 1k test prompts (you'll share a de-identified set).
- Metrics: accuracy (intent/slot match), token-level ROUGE, latency p50/p95, and qualitative error cases.
- Owners: Ben Carter (trial project lead), Marissa Cole (solutions engineer, handles model tuning), Aditya Rao (runtime/ops, infra setup).

3) Model selection (initial recommendation):
- Primary: Llama2-13B-chat (balanced for instruction-following and multilingual quality).
- Fallback: Mistral-7B-Instruct quantized (lower-cost, still good performance; will be used for burst/overflow).
- Notes: if you need heavier multilingual weighting we can try a 13B multilingual-tuned variant in week 2.

4) Timeline (proposed):
- 10/11: Kick-off tech setup + credentials exchange.
- 10/15: MOP (mutual action plan) and test data delivery (ACME).
- 10/18-10/25: Trial runs and evaluation.
- 10/27: Review findings + next-phase proposal.

5) Next steps (for this week):
- ACME: share de-identified 1k prompt set and preferred evaluation labels by 10/15.
- Redwood: share MOP and model-comparison CSV (attached) and spin up trial endpoints.

Attaching a first-pass MOP and the initial model comparison CSV.

[Attachment: acme-poc-mop-v1.pdf (PDF, 72KB)]
[Attachment: model-comparison.csv (CSV, 8KB)]

If that looks good I can schedule the tech kick-off for Monday.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Carolyn Wu <carolyn@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC Trial: model selection & evaluation plan

Thanks Ben — helpful recap. A few clarifications before we lock dates: 

- Multilingual: yes, English + French + Spanish are required. French prompts will include some technical support jargon.
- Latency: can you confirm the p95 target above is measured from an application-level call (end-to-end)? We care about network + runtime.
- Data security: we'll need to confirm this trial runs in a private VPC or on dedicated capacity; can Redwood support that for the duration of the trial? If not, we need a written assurance of no retention of customer data.
- Fallback model: is Mistral-7B quantized expected to keep the same API surface? Will there be observable output differences we should flag to product?

I can share the 1k prompts but need to de-identify them first; aiming to deliver by 10/15. Also looping in our procurement contact (copied below) to fast-track the trial NDA.

Thanks — Carolyn
Carolyn Wu
Head of Product Operations
ACME Corp

[Procurement: procurement@acme.com]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Carolyn Wu <carolyn@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-08T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC Trial: model selection & evaluation plan

Carolyn — great questions, thanks. Answers below and an adjusted plan: 

- Latency measurement: we'll measure end-to-end from an application-level HTTP call to the Redwood trial endpoint (includes network + runtime). We'll provide p50/p95 and the test harness we use so you can replicate.

- Private capacity / data handling: for the trial we can offer a dedicated trial pool (no multi-tenant sharing) and we will enable 'no retention' mode for customer payloads during the trial. Aditya will own infra & compliance checks.

- Fallback model differences: the API surface will be identical. There will be stylistic and output-quality differences between Llama2-13B-chat and Mistral-7B-Instruct; we recommend marking the fallback behavior in the UI for transparency during the trial. Marissa will help tune prompts to reduce regressions.

Updated evaluation plan (concrete metrics):
- Test set: 1,000 prompts (approx 400 EN, 300 FR, 300 ES) provided by ACME.
- Metrics: intent F1, token ROUGE, exact-match for canonical responses where applicable, p50/p95 latency, and business-acceptance % (manual spot-check).
- Targets: F1 >= 0.78 overall; per-language delta <= 5% vs EN; p95 <= 800ms.

Owners & timeline (confirmed):
- Ben Carter: overall trial lead + customer coordination.
- Marissa Cole: prompt engineering, QA sampling, and tuning.
- Aditya Rao: infra, dedicated pool, monitoring dashboards.

Schedule:
- 10/11: Tech kick-off (30m) — Aditya to confirm endpoint details.
- 10/15: ACME delivers de-identified prompts + sign NDA.
- 10/18-10/25: Trial runs (we'll run at least 3 full passes with different prompt templating).
- 10/26: Internal analysis.
- 10/27: Joint review call.

Next steps for this thread: 
- I'll send calendar invites for 10/11 kick-off and 10/27 review.
- Marissa: can you prepare a short tuning checklist and the prompt templates we'll try?

Attached is an updated model-comparison CSV with expected latency and estimated cost per 1k tokens for the recommended models.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Ben

[Attachment: model-comparison.csv (CSV, 9KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Carolyn Wu <carolyn@acme.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-09T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC Trial: model selection & evaluation plan

Carolyn — I'll take point on the prompt templates and the tuning checklist. Tentative plan:

- I'll share a 1-page prompt engineering checklist by 10/11 morning.
- I'll prepare two template variants for each language (EN/FR/ES) so we can run the 3-pass evaluation Ben mentioned.
- I'll run a quick sanity run on 50 prompts once ACME shares the de-identified set to flag any immediate quality regressions.

Ben / Aditya — I'll coordinate with you to schedule the 10/11 kick-off and will include notes about the dedicated pool and the 'no retention' mode so procurement is comfortable.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
